messages:
pagerduty: :rotating_light: P1 - Serving runtime OOM surge in us-west-2. Rapid autoscale activity observed leading to node flaps and container crashloops. Symptoms: CUDA OOM in inference-runtime containers, kubelet restarts, 5xx spike ~18%. Pager: https://pager.example/INC-12345

kai: taking this, on-call ack

kai: quick summary from nodes - autoscaler bounced from ~80 -> 160 -> 70 within ~10m. Seeing many CrashLoopBackOff on inference-runtime pods. Attaching recent pod list and tail of logs:

```
kubectl get pods -n inference | egrep "inference-runtime.*CrashLoopBackOff"
inference-runtime-5f6d7  CrashLoopBackOff  2/3  0  3m

kubectl logs inference-runtime-5f6d7 -n inference -c runtime
2026-03-15T07:11:02 ERROR CUDA: out of memory when allocating 2.1GiB
2026-03-15T07:11:03 FATAL container died: signal 6
```

chloe: customer impact? which customers seeing errors?

kai: Impact is real: overall API 5xx up, some requests falling back to CPU replicas (high latency). No data loss. Errors concentrated on long sequence lengths and some larger-model routes.

jules: Any recent rollout that could correlate? new kernels, quantization changes?

kai: Yes — canary of runtime v2.3 with a low-precision compiled kernel rolled out yesterday to 10% then auto-increased via scaling policies. It looks like under certain seq_len distributions the low-precision kernels allocate more transient GPU memory -> OOM on some instance types. Autoscaler bounce amplified the situation.

maya: mitigation proposal: 1) freeze autoscaler (prevent further scale-up/down), 2) scale to a safe fixed capacity (~140 GPU pods), 3) cordon and drain the most flappy nodes, 4) roll back canary to v2.2.

oncall-bot: executing: kubectl get hpa -n inference --show-labels

kai: applying manual replica patch to stop autoscaler pressure now:

```
kubectl -n inference patch deployment inference-runtime -p '{"spec":{"replicas":140}}'
```

infra-bot: node cordon executed: node-usw2-az3-7 cordoned by infra-bot.

jules: can we route non-critical traffic to a smaller model (redwood-small) to reduce gpu memory pressure?

kai: started traffic policy change: updating routing table to bias non-SLA keys -> redwood-small. This should reduce per-request memory with minimal customer impact.

chloe: current known impacted customers: Acme Corp (30% error rate spike), Finch Health (degraded inference latency), BetaDocs (intermittent 500s). Estimated first-seen ~07:10 UTC, peak ~07:15-07:20.

maya: I'll draft a status page update: "We're mitigating an autoscaler-induced GPU OOM issue in us-west-2 affecting some inference requests. Engineers are stabilizing capacity and rolling back a recent runtime canary. ETA 30m for stabilization."

kai: rollback to v2.2 canary disabled and rollout started. Restarting pods now. Early indicators: crashloop count dropping (was 37 -> now 4). :white_check_mark:

kai: recent pod logs after restart look better:

```
2026-03-15T07:24:10 INFO runtime initialized, gpu mem available 15.8GiB
2026-03-15T07:24:11 INFO serving loop ready
```

jules: for post-incident: add seq_length gating in compilation path, mem-safety limits for low-precision kernels, and autoscaler damping (min window) so we don't bounce. Also consider per-model resource guzzling mitigation (OOM sentinel + failover).

maya: agreed. immediate config change: set autoscaler min-stable-window=5m and max-scale-step to reduce rapid swings.

sre-lead: thanks team. Good containment. Please create full postmortem with timeline, root cause (kernel memory regression + autoscaler amplification), impacted customer list, and remediation plan. I'll take the handoff for follow-up tasks. @kai @jules please add notes to the incidents doc and schedule a runtime retro.

kai: will add detailed notes and link CI artifacts.

chloe: I'll prepare customer comms and update status once we confirm steady metrics. :memo:

maya: closing on-call actions, keeping this thread for postmortem follow-up. :thumbsup:
